proof:
Ignore the boundary of $A$, which has zero volume. At $x\in\operatorname{int}A$, images of sufficiently small closed balls about $x$ have the same volume as the balls: the images are compact, $T$ is injective, and its pushforward is uniform volume on $D$. Differentiability at $x$ puts such an image inside $T(x)+r[DT(x)\overline B_1+\varepsilon(r)\overline B_1]$, where $\overline B_1$ is the unit ball and $\varepsilon(r)\to0$. Taking volumes divided by $r^d$ and using continuity from above of these shrinking neighborhoods gives $\det DT(x)\ge1$, including exclusion of singular derivatives. For $S=(1-\theta)\operatorname{Id}+\theta T$, the nonnegative eigenvalues of $DT(x)$ and weighted arithmetic–geometric mean therefore give $\det DS(x)\ge(\det DT(x))^\theta\ge1$.

Monotonicity gives $(S(x)-S(x'))\cdot(x-x')\ge(1-\theta)|x-x'|^2$, so $S$ is injective and its inverse on its image is $(1-\theta)^{-1}$-Lipschitz. In particular the pushforward is absolutely continuous, since the inverse sends Lebesgue-null subsets of its image to null sets. For $y=S(x)$ with $x$ in the interior, the inverse Lipschitz bound and differentiability of $S$ at $x$ give, uniformly for $z$ in the image within distance $r$ of $y$,
$$
DS(x)(S^{-1}(z)-x)=(z-y)+o(r).
$$
Thus the preimage of the radius-$r$ ball about $y$ is contained in $x+DS(x)^{-1}B(0,r+o(r))$, and its volume divided by the ball volume has limsup at most $(\det DS(x))^{-1}\le1$. Lebesgue differentiation gives density at most one on the image of the interior, which is a countable union of images of compact subsets of the interior and carries the entire pushforward. The two values of $\theta$ interpolate to integer bases $0,1$, respectively, so convexity puts both images in their actual common fiber $B$.

For the failure without monotonicity, take all fibers in the product $[-k,k+1]\times B$ with $B=-B$, and apply $T(x)=-x$ on the endpoints. Both endpoints retain volume; the two interpolants are linear scalings by $1/(2k+1)$ and $-1/(2k+1)$. Each has density $(2k+1)^d$ on a positive-volume image inside $B$.
statement: Let $k\ge1$ and let $A,D$ be equal-positive-volume convex bodies in the actual endpoint fibers at $-k,k+1$ of a convex source whose two middle fibers at $0,1$ are the same body $B$. Suppose a specified injective monotone map $T:A\to D$ differentiable on $\operatorname{int}A$, with symmetric positive semidefinite derivative there, pushes Lebesgue volume on $A$ onto Lebesgue volume on $D$. For $\theta=k/(2k+1),(k+1)/(2k+1)$, the map $(1-\theta)\operatorname{Id}+\theta T$ sends volume on $A$ to a measure with density at most $\mathbf1_B$. Arbitrary volume-preserving maps can fail: for $A=D=B=-B$ and $T(x)=-x$, both output densities are $(2k+1)^d$ on their images.
title: Unit interpolation density for a specified differentiable monotone endpoint map
